# Nearline MiniOneRec: simulated A/B and freshness

<!-- Generated by `make nearline-report` (analysis/nearline_report.py). Do not edit by hand. -->

MiniOneRec does not run on the request path: one 50-beam request takes 3.1 s on this Mac, 0.64 s with the prompt encoded once (minionerec.md, Cost), against the feed's 100 ms budget. It runs nearline (design §11 step 5): a history change queues the user (apply.lua, in the same script as the history update), the worker generates once the history has been quiet for 30 s (at most 120 s after the first unanswered change), writes the top 50 items to the state Redis, and the home feed fuses them as a fourth RRF source (`gen`) when the user has a result.

## Setup

- Bundle `2026-11-08-sasrec64-ce60bf5d`; generator `minionerec-365a03fc-b50` (mps, bfloat16, 50 beams, prompt encoded once, batches of up to 2).
- Experiment `recall-gen-ab-v1` in the recall layer, 50 / 50 over all users: control = RRF sasrec 1, itemcf 1, pop 0.3; gen = RRF sasrec 1, itemcf 1, pop 0.3, gen 1. The gen weight was fixed beforehand (SASRec's and ItemCF's), not tuned. The recall layer's running experiments (`recall-rrf-weights-v1`) were stopped for the phase and restored afterwards. Both arms are ordered by RRF: the LightGBM ranker was trained on the three sources' features only (an item only gen returned has none of them), so the rank layer ran no experiment.
- Traffic: 60 min, 4 sessions at a time with pauses of 50-300 ms between page views (23,684 sessions, 76,878 page views), fewer than M4's 16 so that the worker keeps up. Standing campaigns fill the sponsored slots.
- Start: consumers caught up, Redis reseeded with the dataset users' training histories, then the worker generated the gen arm's 1,026 users from them (backfill: 7.4 min) before the traffic started. The worker generates only for the gen arm's users.
- State Redis: 0 evicted, 0 refused writes, 105.4 MB used at the end; cache Redis: 0 evicted, 0 refused writes, 68.1 MB used at the end.

## Split

2,024 users: control 998, gen 1,026; chi-square p = 0.534; 0 users in two arms; 0 users whose arm differs from the Python bucketing (sound).

## Latency

| Arm | Requests | Client P50 (ms) | Client P99 (ms) | Degraded | Candidate cache hit rate (home, first pages) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| control | 37,202 | 5.0 | 14.7 | 0.35% | 74.9% |
| gen | 39,675 | 5.1 | 15.0 | 0.37% | 73.4% |

The gen arm reads its result in the same Redis round trip as the rest of the user context. Its candidate cache key carries the result's history version, so a new result is used by the next request instead of waiting out the cache's 5 minutes; that costs the gen arm one more cache miss per written result.

## Freshness

- History change applied → result written: P50 31.0 s, P90 32.1 s, P99 48.3 s, max 80.3 s (3,804).
- The event itself → result written: P50 31.0 s, P90 32.1 s, P99 48.3 s, max 80.3 s (3,804).
- Changes answered per generation: P50 1.0 changes, P90 3.0 changes, P99 6.0 changes, max 10.0 changes (2,283); due → claimed (time in the queue after the debounce): P50 0.2 s, P90 0.6 s, P99 1.2 s, max 2.7 s (2,283).
- Queue: at most 58 users queued and 3 due at once during the traffic; 1 due at the end.
- The gen arm's home first pages: fresh 80.6%, missing 9.3%, stale 9.8%, unavailable 0.3% of 31,957; stale by 1 version: 2,179, 2 versions: 542, 3 versions: 233, 4 versions: 107, 5 versions: 29, 6 versions: 22, 7 versions: 3, 10 versions: 1. Age of the result when served: P50 827.8 s, P90 2,316.9 s, P99 3,564.2 s, max 4,029.6 s (28,881).
- For scale: a simulated user comes back after P50 204.9 s, P90 649.7 s, P99 1,259.2 s, max 2,833.9 s (20,879) (page views more than 10 s apart). The simulator compresses time; against real visit gaps of hours the debounce and the generation time would be small.

## Worker

- 3,049 users generated in 2,140 batches, 0.68 s per user of generation; generator setup 5 s; peak footprint of the generator 8.0 GiB (MPS capped at 8 GB); job statuses: written 3,049, no_history 260.
- 1-minute load 2.5 at the start, 1.8 at the end; swapped out while it ran: 1.4 GiB.
